<odoo>
  <data>
    <menuitem name="CMS" id="menu_cms_root"/>
    <menuitem name="Settings" id="menu_cms_settings" parent="menu_cms_root" sequence="900"/>

    <!-- ============================================================ -->
    <!-- Client Action for SIM GKI Dashboard                          -->
    <!-- ============================================================ -->
    <record id="sim_gki_dashboard_client_action" model="ir.actions.client">
        <field name="name">Dashboard SIM GKI</field>
        <field name="tag">sim_gki_dashboard</field>
    </record>

    <!-- Top menu item -->
    <menuitem name="SIM GKI" 
                id="church_base.menu_root"
          web_icon="church_base/static/src/img/icon.png"
            groups="church_base.group_cms_member_user,church_base.group_cms_litbang"
            action="sim_gki_dashboard_client_action"
                />

    <!-- Dashboard as first menu item -->
    <menuitem name="🏠 Dashboard" 
                id="church_base.menu_dashboard" 
            parent="church_base.menu_root"
            action="sim_gki_dashboard_client_action"
            sequence="1"/>

    <!-- menu categories -->
    <menuitem name="Anggota Jemaat" 
                id="church_base.jemaat_anggota" 
            parent="church_base.menu_root"
            sequence="10"/>
    <menuitem name="Konfigurasi" 
                id="church_base.configuration" 
            parent="church_base.menu_root"
            sequence="15"/>

    <!-- actions -->

    <!-- menu categories -->
    <menuitem name="Pengaturan" 
                id="church_base.jemaat_pengaturan" 
            parent="church_base.menu_root"
          sequence="999"
          />

    <menuitem name="Bidang & Komisi" 
                id="church_base.jemaat_pengaturan_bidangkomisi" 
            parent="church_base.jemaat_pengaturan"/>

    <menuitem name="Sosial Demografi" 
                id="church_base.jemaat_pengaturan_sosialdemografi" 
            parent="church_base.jemaat_pengaturan"/>

    <menuitem name="Struktur Organisasi" 
                id="church_base.jemaat_pengaturan_lainlain" 
            parent="church_base.jemaat_pengaturan"
            sequence="10"/>

    <!-- menu categories -->
    <menuitem name="Pergumulan" 
                id="church_base.jemaat_pergumulan" 
            parent="church_base.menu_root"
          sequence="200"
          />


  </data>
</odoo>

<odoo>
    <data noupdate="0">

            Tim Litbang: READ access to evaluation data scoped by admin_user_ids hierarchy.

            via admin_user_ids on the respective entity (jemaat, klasis, sinodewilayah, sinode).

checkpoint.userIntent:
Implementing Readonly Litbang Group

The user's main objective is to implement a new "readonly" access control tier for the Litbang (Research & Development) group in Odoo 16. The specific goals are:
1. Create a `group_cms_litbang_readonly` group with strictly read-only permissions across all relevant church management and evaluation models.
2. Restructure the security hierarchy so that the standard `group_cms_litbang` (which has partial write/dashboard management access) inherits from this new readonly group.
3. Update security rules (access rules and record rules) and menu visibility to ensure users in the new group can navigate the system and view data without possessing any write, create, or unlink privileges.
4. Integrate the new security group into all existing evaluation menus and dashboard views to maintain consistent access control across the church management system.
checkpoint.sessionSummary:
### Summary of Implementation: Creating Read-Only Litbang Access

The user requested a new Odoo 16 group, `group_cms_litbang_readonly`, to provide read-only access to existing Litbang features. I restructured the existing Litbang group hierarchy to ensure proper permission inheritance and security scope.

#### Key Changes & Design Decisions
1.  **Hierarchy Restructuring:**
    *   Created `group_cms_litbang_readonly` (new tier).
    *   Modified `group_cms_litbang` to inherit from `group_cms_litbang_readonly`.
    *   `group_cms_litbang_manager` continues to inherit from `group_cms_litbang`.
2.  **Access Control:**
    *   **Model Access (`ir.model.access.csv`):** Added `perm_read=1, perm_write=0, perm_create=0, perm_unlink=0` rules for the `litbang_readonly` group across all relevant modules (`church_base`, `church_dashboard`, `church_evaluation`).
    *   **Record Rules (`ir.rule`):** Implemented new record rules in `litbang_security.xml` for `group_cms_litbang_readonly`. These rules mirror the existing Litbang scoping (using `admin_user_ids` hierarchy) to ensure that readonly users only see data for their assigned entities (Jemaat/Klasis/SW).
3.  **Menu & Navigation Visibility:**
    *   Updated the `SIM GKI` root menu and the evaluation module's `Dashboard` and `Tahun` menus to include the `group_cms_litbang_readonly` group, ensuring authorized readonly users can see and navigate to these modules.

#### Implementation Locations
*   `/church_base/security/group.xml`: Group definitions and hierarchy.
*   `/church_base/security/ir.model.access.csv`: Base access rules.
*   `/church_base/views/main_menu.xml`: Root menu visibility.
*   `/church_dashboard/security/ir.model.access.csv`: Dashboard access rules.
*   `/church_evaluation/security/ir.model.access.csv`: Evaluation access rules.
*   `/church_evaluation/security/litbang_security.xml`: Record rules for scoping.
*   `/church_evaluation/views/evaluation_dashboard_views.xml`: Dashboard menu visibility.
*   `/church_evaluation/views/fiscalyear_views.xml`: Yearly evaluation menu visibility.

#### Dependencies & Context
*   The system uses the `church_base` module as the source of truth for Litbang groups.
*   The implementation assumes Odoo 16's standard `eval="[(4, ref('...'))]"` group inheritance pattern.
*   No changes were made to existing controllers or business logic; access is strictly enforced via Odoo's native security layer.

#### Next Steps
*   **Verification:** Deploy these changes to the Odoo environment and restart the server to refresh security metadata.
*   **Testing:** Assign a test user to the `Tim Litbang - Readonly` group to confirm they can view the dashboard/PURJ data but are denied write/create/delete actions (e.g., test saving a record or editing a field).
*   **Sync:** Ensure that `ir.model.access` and `ir.rule` updates are successfully loaded by Odoo (may require a module upgrade of `church_base` and `church_evaluation`).

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<odoo>
    <data noupdate="0">
        <!--
            Tim Litbang: READ access to evaluation data scoped by admin_user_ids hierarchy.
            Litbang users can read evaluation data for jemaat/klasis/SW they are assigned to

Extracting OpenERP Receivable Balances

The user's main objective is to extract Accounts Receivable (AR) balances per 31 December 2025 from their OpenERP 6.1 server. Goals include:

2. Developing an efficient reporting pipeline that uses server-side aggregation (`read_group`) to handle millions of journal items without locking the database.
3. Decoupling report execution into two phases: a fast, account-level summary for immediate insights and a chunked, offline-safe process for granular partner-level detail.
4. Exporting structured results (JSON and CSV) for offline analysis.

## Selesai ✅

Group **"Tim Litbang - Readonly"** (`group_cms_litbang_readonly`) sudah dibuat dengan hierarki 3-tier:

1. **Tim Litbang - Readonly** → Read-only saja pada semua model
2. **Tim Litbang** → Mewarisi readonly + write pada dashboard  
3. **Tim Litbang - Manager** → Mewarisi litbang + write pada evaluasi

| Komponen | Detail |
|----------|--------|
| **Group definition** | `church_base/security/group.xml` |
| **ir.model.access** | 4 baris di `church_base` + 21 baris di `church_evaluation` + 2 baris di `church_dashboard` — semua `1,0,0,0` (read only) |
| **ir.rule** | 6 record rules di `litbang_security.xml` — scoping berdasarkan `admin_user_ids` hierarchy (sama persis dengan litbang biasa) |
| **Menu visibility** | ~17 menu items di seluruh modul sudah ditambahkan `group_cms_litbang_readonly` |

### Cara deploy:

```bash
./odoo-bin -u church_base,church_evaluation,church_dashboard -d <database>
```

Setelah update, assign group **"Tim Litbang - Readonly"** ke user melalui **Settings → Users → Access Rights**.

plannerResponse.thinking:
The user wants to break down the Litbang Readonly group into three sub-groups based on organizational scope:
1. **Litbang Klasis** — can only see data at the Klasis level and below
2. **Litbang Sinode Wilayah** — can see data at the Sinode Wilayah level and below
3. **Litbang Sinode** — can see data at the Sinode level (everything)

This is a great idea for fine-grained access control. Let me think about the architecture:

Currently the `litbang_readonly` group uses `ir.rule` domain filters based on `admin_user_ids` hierarchy. 

I see now — the scoping is already determined by which entity the user is assigned to through `admin_user_ids`, but the user wants to formalize this into distinct groups where each level has its own readonly role with appropriate domain filters. So I need to create three separate groups with rules that respect the organizational hierarchy: Klasis-level users see only their klasis and jemaat, Sinode Wilayah users see their region and everything below it, and Sinode users get full visibility. ir.rule` already handles scoping via `admin_user_ids`. If a user is assigned as admin on a klasis, they can see klasis-level data and jemaat-level data under that klasis. If assigned on a sinode wilayah, they see SW + klasis + jemaat under it.

So the real distinction is between which models they can access versus which records they're scoped to see. The system has evaluations at three levels: jemaat, klasis, and sinode wilayah. I'm thinking the role hierarchy should reflect this—Litbang Klasis can read jemaat and klasis evaluations within their assigned klasis, Litbang Sinode Wilayah inherits that and adds SW-level evaluations, and Litbang Sinode gets everything. This creates a clean hierarchy where each level builds on the previous one, and then the existing litbang groups layer on top for write permissions. I'm sketching out a hierarchical group structure where each tier inherits permissions from the level below—klasis litbang can see jemaat and klasis data, sinode wilayah adds SW-level visibility, and sinode litbang sees everything. But I'm realizing the existing `group_cms_litbang` already handles write access, so I need to figure out how these readonly tiers fit into the current permission model. I'm realizing I need to reconsider how Odoo's access control actually works in practice, rather than just mapping out the group hierarchy.

Since access rights are cumulative, I can leverage inheritance efficiently: litbang_sw inherits from litbang_klasis and gains all its model access plus additional SW-specific models. For record-level security, I'm setting up ir.rules that scope access based on the relationship between records and the user's administrative domain—so litbang_klasis users see jemaat and klasis evaluations only for their assigned klasis, while litbang_sw users get broader access through their SW scope.

The tricky part is that Odoo ORs together rules for the same model across different groups, so a user with both litbang_klasis and litbang_sw would see the union of both rule sets—which is actually what I want, since they'd have access to everything their roles permit.

But I need to be careful about the inheritance chain: a litbang_sw user inherits litbang_klasis, so they should see klasis-scoped data plus SW-scoped data. A litbang_klasis user should only see klasis-scoped data. The rules need to reflect this properly without accidentally granting too much access.

Let me look at the existing litbang_readonly rules to understand the current pattern... for jemaat evaluations check:

checkpoint.userIntent:
Implementing Granular Litbang Access

The user's main objective is to decompose the monolithic "Tim Litbang - Readonly" group into specific, role-based tiers for "Klasis", "Sinode Wilayah", and "Sinode" levels. The goal is to provide granular read-only access that enforces strict organizational scoping, ensuring users can only view evaluation data and analytics relevant to their specific administrative hierarchy within the church management system.
checkpoint.sessionSummary:
### Summary of Implementation: Readonly Litbang Group

In this session, I successfully implemented a new **"Readonly" access control tier** for the Litbang (Research & Development) group in Odoo 16. This was achieved by restructuring the group hierarchy to enforce stricter permissions while maintaining compatibility with the existing system.

#### Key Implementation Details
1.  **Group Hierarchy Restructuring:**
    *   **`group_cms_litbang_readonly`**: Created as the base tier for read-only access.
    *   **`group_cms_litbang`**: Modified to inherit from `group_cms_litbang_readonly` (implied group).
    *   **`group_cms_litbang_manager`**: Retained at the top of the hierarchy, inheriting from `group_cms_litbang`.
2.  **Security Rules & Access Control:**
    *   **`ir.model.access.csv`**: Updated base and evaluation module security files to grant `perm_read=1` (with `write/create/unlink=0`) to the new readonly group for all critical models (Jemaat, Klasis, Sinode Wilayah, and Evaluation measures/values).
    *   **`ir.rule` (Record Rules)**: Implemented new scoped rules for the readonly group in `litbang_security.xml`, mirroring the `admin_user_ids` hierarchy used by the standard Litbang group. This ensures data scoping is correctly enforced for readonly users.
3.  **UI & Navigation:**
    *   Updated the `SIM GKI` root menu and all sub-menus within `church_evaluation` and `church_dashboard` (e.g., PURJ, Pengukuran, Tahun, Klasis/SW Evaluation) to include the `group_cms_litbang_readonly` in the `groups` attribute, ensuring visibility for authorized users.

#### Summary of Modified Files
*   `church_base/security/group.xml`: Group definitions and hierarchy setup.
*   `church_base/security/ir.model.access.csv`: Added base ACLs.
*   `church_evaluation/security/ir.model.access.csv`: Added evaluation-specific ACLs.
*   `church_evaluation/security/litbang_security.xml`: Added domain-based record rules.
*   Various view files (`jemaat_measure_views.xml`, `fiscalyear_views.xml`, etc.): Updated menu visibility.

#### Context for Future Work
*   **Next Steps (User Request):** The user has requested a further breakdown of the Litbang role based on organizational scope: **Litbang Klasis**, **Litbang Sinode Wilayah**, and **Litbang Sinode**.
*   **Security Design:** The current system uses `admin_user_ids` on the entities themselves for data scoping. Any future organizational breakdown must continue to respect this domain-based filtering to ensure data isolation.
*   **Deployment:** The changes require a module upgrade (`-u church_base,church_evaluation,church_dashboard`) followed by assigning the new groups to relevant users in the Odoo backend.

This implementation provides a solid foundation for the requested organizational scoping. Any future work should focus on defining the granular groups and updating `ir.rule` domains to reflect the new organizational boundaries.

# Group Litbang Readonly — Ringkasan Perubahan ## Hierarki Group Baru (3-tier) ```mermaid graph TD A["🔒 Tim Litbang - Readonly
group_cms_litbang_readonly
Read-only semua model"] --> B["📊 Tim Litbang
group_cms_litbang
+ Write dashboard config/items"] B --> C["🔧 Tim Litbang - Manager
group_cms_litbang_manager
+ Write evaluation data"] ``` | Group | XML ID | Akses | |-------|--------|-------| | **Readonly** | `church_base.group_cms_litbang_readonly` | Read saja pada semua model (jemaat, evaluasi, dashboard, dsb). Tidak bisa create/write/delete. | | **Litbang** | `church_base.group_cms_litbang` | Mewarisi readonly + write pada dashboard config & items. | | **Manager** | `church_base.group_cms_litbang_manager` | Mewarisi litbang + write pada measure values & evaluations. | ## File yang Diubah ### 1. `church_base/security/group.xml` - ✅ Ditambahkan record `group_cms_litbang_readonly` - ✅ `group_cms_litbang` sekarang `implied_ids` → `group_cms_litbang_readonly` ### 2. `church_base/security/ir.model.access.csv` - ✅ Ditambahkan 4 baris readonly untuk: `jemaat_jemaat`, `jemaat_klasis`, `jemaat_sinodewilayah`, `jemaat_sinode` ### 3. `church_base/views/main_menu.xml` - ✅ Menu "SIM GKI" ditambahkan `group_cms_litbang_readonly` ### 4. `church_evaluation/security/ir.model.access.csv` - ✅ Ditambahkan 21 baris readonly untuk semua model evaluasi (measures, values, fiscal year evaluations, sections, charts, narratives) ### 5. `church_evaluation/security/litbang_security.xml` - ✅ Ditambahkan 6 `ir.rule` record rules untuk readonly group (same admin_user_ids scoping) ### 6. `church_dashboard/security/ir.model.access.csv` - ✅ Ditambahkan 2 baris readonly untuk `dashboard_config` dan `dashboard_item` ### 7. Menu Views (semua ditambahkan `group_cms_litbang_readonly`) - `evaluation_dashboard_views.xml` — Dashboard Progress PURJ - `jemaat_measure_value_views.xml` — PURJ, Pengukuran (3 menu items) - `jemaat_measure_views.xml` — Evaluasi/PURJ root, Pengukuran (2 menu items) - `fiscalyear_views.xml` — Tahun - `jemaat_fiscalyear_evaluation_views.xml` — PURJ - `klasis_evaluation_views.xml` — 4 menu items - `sw_evaluation_views.xml` — 4 menu items - `slide_documentation_views.xml` — Dokumentasi Slide ## Cara Deploy ```bash # Restart Odoo dan update modul ./odoo-bin -u church_base,church_evaluation,church_dashboard -d ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > Setelah update modul, assign group **"Tim Litbang - Readonly"** ke user yang diinginkan melalui menu **Settings → Users & Companies → Users → Tab Access Rights**.

Extracting OpenERP Receivable Balances

2. Developing an efficient reporting pipeline that uses server-side aggregation (`read_group`) to handle millions of journal items without locking the database.

<odoo>
  <data>
    <menuitem name="CMS" id="menu_cms_root"/>

    <!-- Client Action for SIM GKI Dashboard                          -->

    <record id="sim_gki_dashboard_client_action" model="ir.actions.client">
        <field name="name">Dashboard SIM GKI</field>
        <field name="tag">sim_gki_dashboard</field>
    </record>

                id="church_base.menu_root"
          web_icon="church_base/static/src/img/icon.png"
            groups="church_base.group_cms_member_user,church_base.group_cms_litbang,church_base.group_cms_litbang_readonly"

                />

                id="church_base.menu_dashboard" 
            parent="church_base.menu_root"
            action="sim_gki_dashboard_client_action"
            sequence="1"/>

                id="church_base.jemaat_anggota" 
            parent="church_base.menu_root"
            sequence="10"/>

            parent="church_base.menu_root"

toolCalls.name: replace_file_content
toolCalls.argumentsJson:
{"AllowMultiple":false,"Description":"Replace the single-group readonly rules with properly scoped ir.rules per group level. Each group gets record rules scoped to their organizational level via admin_user_ids. In Odoo, ir.rules for the same model across different groups are OR'd, so a user with litbang_sinodewilayah (who inherits litbang_klasis) gets BOTH sets of rules combined — seeing records from klasis-level AND SW-level assignments.","EndLine":217,"Instruction":"Replace litbang_ro_* rules with scoped rules per group (klasis, sinodewilayah, sinode)","ReplacementContent":"        <!--
            ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
            LITBANG KLASIS (Readonly): Scoped to klasis-level admin_user_ids.
            User sees jemaat evaluations within their assigned klasis,
            and klasis evaluations for their assigned klasis.
            ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
        -->

        <!-- Litbang Klasis: Jemaat evaluations scoped by klasis admin -->
        <record id="litbang_kls_jemaat_fiscalyear_eval_read" model="ir.rule">
            <field name="name">Litbang Klasis: Read jemaat evaluations (klasis scope)</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="model_jemaat_fiscalyear_evaluation"/>
            <field name="domain_force">[
                '|',
                ('jemaat_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id]),
                ('jemaat_id.klasis_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id])
            ]</field>
            <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('church_base.group_cms_litbang_klasis'))]"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_write" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_unlink" eval="False"/>
        </record>

        <!-- Litbang Klasis: Jemaat measure values scoped by klasis admin -->
        <record id="litbang_kls_jemaat_measure_value_read" model="ir.rule">
            <field name="name">Litbang Klasis: Read jemaat measure values (klasis scope)</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="model_jemaat_measure_value"/>
            <field name="domain_force">[
                '|',
                ('jemaat_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id]),
                ('jemaat_id.klasis_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id])
            ]</field>
            <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('church_base.group_cms_litbang_klasis'))]"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_write" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_unlink" eval="False"/>
        </record>

        <!-- Litbang Klasis: Klasis evaluations scoped by klasis admin -->
        <record id="litbang_kls_klasis_fiscalyear_eval_read" model="ir.rule">
            <field name="name">Litbang Klasis: Read klasis evaluations (klasis scope)</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="model_klasis_fiscalyear_evaluation"/>
            <field name="domain_force">[
                ('klasis_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id])
            ]</field>
            <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('church_base.group_cms_litbang_klasis'))]"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_write" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_unlink" eval="False"/>
        </record>

        <!-- Litbang Klasis: Klasis measure values scoped by klasis admin -->
        <record id="litbang_kls_klasis_measure_value_read" model="ir.rule">
            <field name="name">Litbang Klasis: Read klasis measure values (klasis scope)</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="model_klasis_measure_value"/>
            <field name="domain_force">[
                ('klasis_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id])
            ]</field>
            <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('church_base.group_cms_litbang_klasis'))]"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_write" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_unlink" eval="False"/>
        </record>

        <!--
            ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
            LITBANG SINODE WILAYAH (Readonly): Scoped to SW-level admin_user_ids.
            Adds SW-level record rules. Combined with inherited klasis rules
            via OR logic, user sees records from both klasis AND SW assignments.
            ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
        -->

        <!-- Litbang SW: Jemaat evaluations scoped by SW admin -->
        <record id="litbang_sw_jemaat_fiscalyear_eval_read" model="ir.rule">
            <field name="name">Litbang SW: Read jemaat evaluations (SW scope)</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="model_jemaat_fiscalyear_evaluation"/>
            <field name="domain_force">[
                ('jemaat_id.sinodewilayah_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id])
            ]</field>
            <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('church_base.group_cms_litbang_sinodewilayah'))]"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_write" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_unlink" eval="False"/>
        </record>

        <!-- Litbang SW: Jemaat measure values scoped by SW admin -->
        <record id="litbang_sw_jemaat_measure_value_read" model="ir.rule">
            <field name="name">Litbang SW: Read jemaat measure values (SW scope)</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="model_jemaat_measure_value"/>
            <field name="domain_force">[
                ('jemaat_id.sinodewilayah_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id])
            ]</field>
            <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('church_base.group_cms_litbang_sinodewilayah'))]"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_write" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_unlink" eval="False"/>
        </record>

        <!-- Litbang SW: Klasis evaluations scoped by SW admin -->
        <record id="litbang_sw_klasis_fiscalyear_eval_read" model="ir.rule">
            <field name="name">Litbang SW: Read klasis evaluations (SW scope)</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="model_klasis_fiscalyear_evaluation"/>
            <field name="domain_force">[
                ('klasis_id.sinodewilayah_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id])
            ]</field>
            <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('church_base.group_cms_litbang_sinodewilayah'))]"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_write" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_unlink" eval="False"/>
        </record>

        <!-- Litbang SW: Klasis measure values scoped by SW admin -->
        <record id="litbang_sw_klasis_measure_value_read" model="ir.rule">
            <field name="name">Litbang SW: Read klasis measure values (SW scope)</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="model_klasis_measure_value"/>
            <field name="domain_force">[
                ('klasis_id.sinodewilayah_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id])
            ]</field>
            <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('church_base.group_cms_litbang_sinodewilayah'))]"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_write" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_unlink" eval="False"/>
        </record>

        <!-- Litbang SW: SW evaluations scoped by SW admin -->
        <record id="litbang_sw_sw_fiscalyear_eval_read" model="ir.rule">
            <field name="name">Litbang SW: Read SW evaluations (SW scope)</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="model_sw_fiscalyear_evaluation"/>
            <field name="domain_force">[
                ('sinodewilayah_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id])
            ]</field>
            <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('church_base.group_cms_litbang_sinodewilayah'))]"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_write" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_unlink" eval="False"/>
        </record>

        <!-- Litbang SW: SW measure values scoped by SW admin -->
        <record id="litbang_sw_sw_measure_value_read" model="ir.rule">
            <field name="name">Litbang SW: Read SW measure values (SW scope)</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="model_sw_measure_value"/>
            <field name="domain_force">[
                ('sinodewilayah_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id])
            ]</field>
            <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('church_base.group_cms_litbang_sinodewilayah'))]"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_write" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_unlink" eval="False"/>
        </record>

        <!--
            ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
            LITBANG SINODE (Readonly): Scoped to sinode-level admin_user_ids.
            Adds sinode-level record rules. Combined with inherited SW + klasis
            rules, user can see records from ALL organizational levels.
            ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
        -->

        <!-- Litbang Sinode: Jemaat evaluations scoped by sinode admin -->
        <record id="litbang_sin_jemaat_fiscalyear_eval_read" model="ir.rule">
            <field name="name">Litbang Sinode: Read jemaat evaluations (sinode scope)</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="model_jemaat_fiscalyear_evaluation"/>
            <field name="domain_force">[
                ('jemaat_id.sinode_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id])
            ]</field>
            <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('church_base.group_cms_litbang_sinode'))]"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>

# Group Litbang Readonly — Ringkasan Perubahan ## Hierarki Group Baru (3-tier) ```mermaid graph TD A["🔒 Tim Litbang - Readonly

+ Write evaluation data"] ``` | Group | XML ID | Akses | |-------|--------|-------| | **Readonly** | `church_base.group_cms_litbang_readonly` | Read saja pada semua model (jemaat, evaluasi, dashboard, dsb). Tidak bisa create/write/delete. | | **Litbang** | `church_base.group_cms_litbang` | Mewarisi readonly + write pada dashboard config & items. | | **Manager** | `church_base.group_cms_litbang_manager` | Mewarisi litbang + write pada measure values & evaluations. | ## File yang Diubah ### 1. `church_base/security/group.xml` - ✅ Ditambahkan record `group_cms_litbang_readonly` - ✅ `group_cms_litbang` sekarang `implied_ids` → `group_cms_litbang_readonly` ### 2. `church_base/security/ir.model.access.csv` - ✅ Ditambahkan 4 baris readonly untuk: `jemaat_jemaat`, `jemaat_klasis`, `jemaat_sinodewilayah`, `jemaat_sinode` ### 3. `church_base/views/main_menu.xml` - ✅ Menu "SIM GKI" ditambahkan `group_cms_litbang_readonly` ### 4. `church_evaluation/security/ir.model.access.csv` - ✅ Ditambahkan 21 baris readonly untuk semua model evaluasi (measures, values, fiscal year evaluations, sections, charts, narratives) ### 5. `church_evaluation/security/litbang_security.xml` - ✅ Ditambahkan 6 `ir.rule` record rules untuk readonly group (same admin_user_ids scoping) ### 6. `church_dashboard/security/ir.model.access.csv` - ✅ Ditambahkan 2 baris readonly untuk `dashboard_config` dan `dashboard_item` ### 7. Menu Views (semua ditambahkan `group_cms_litbang_readonly`) - `evaluation_dashboard_views.xml` — Dashboard Progress PURJ - `jemaat_measure_value_views.xml` — PURJ, Pengukuran (3 menu items) - `jemaat_measure_views.xml` — Evaluasi/PURJ root, Pengukuran (2 menu items) - `fiscalyear_views.xml` — Tahun - `jemaat_fiscalyear_evaluation_views.xml` — PURJ - `klasis_evaluation_views.xml` — 4 menu items - `sw_evaluation_views.xml` — 4 menu items - `slide_documentation_views.xml` — Dokumentasi Slide ## Cara Deploy ```bash # Restart Odoo dan update modul ./odoo-bin -u church_base,church_evaluation,church_dashboard -d ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > Setelah update modul, assign group **"Tim Litbang - Readonly"** ke user yang diinginkan melalui menu **Settings → Users & Companies → Users → Tab Access Rights**.

artifactMetadata.summary: Complete documentation of the Litbang group hierarchy refactored into 5 tiers: Litbang Klasis (readonly jemaat+klasis scope) → Litbang Sinode Wilayah (readonly + SW scope) → Litbang Sinode (readonly + sinode scope) → Tim Litbang (write dashboard) → Tim Litbang Manager (write evaluations). Covers group definitions, ir.model.access scoping, ir.rule record rules with layered OR-based domain filtering, and menu visibility mapping.

plannerResponse.response:
## Selesai ✅

Group Litbang sudah di-breakdown menjadi **3 level scope** (readonly) + 2 level write yang sudah ada:

```
🔒 Litbang Klasis          → readonly jemaat + klasis (scoped per klasis)
  ↑ inherited by
🔒 Litbang Sinode Wilayah  → + readonly SW models (scoped per SW)
  ↑ inherited by
🔒 Litbang Sinode           → + readonly sinode-level (lihat semua)
  ↑ inherited by
📊 Tim Litbang              → + write dashboard
  ↑ inherited by
🔧 Tim Litbang Manager     → + write evaluations
```

### Poin penting:
- **ir.rules layered** — tiap level hanya scope ke `admin_user_ids` di levelnya. Odoo menggabungkan rules antar group dengan OR, jadi user SW otomatis bisa lihat data klasis + SW
- **Menu scoped** — Menu SW hanya muncul untuk `litbang_sinodewilayah` ke atas. User `litbang_klasis` hanya lihat menu jemaat + klasis
- **Backward compatible** — `group_cms_litbang` dan `group_cms_litbang_manager` tetap berfungsi normal, sekarang inherit dari `litbang_sinode` (full readonly)

Deploy: `./odoo-bin -u church_base,church_evaluation,church_dashboard -d <database>`

checkpoint.userIntent:
Implementing Granular Litbang Access

The user's main objective is to decompose the monolithic "Tim Litbang" access into tiered, role-based groups ("Klasis", "Sinode Wilayah", and "Sinode") to enforce organizational scoping. The goal is to provide granular read-only access for evaluation data and analytics, ensuring users only view church management data relevant to their administrative hierarchy, while maintaining backend security consistency and UI visibility across the Odoo CMS.
checkpoint.sessionSummary:
### Session Summary: Implementing Granular Litbang Access

In this session, we successfully decomposed the monolithic **"Tim Litbang - Readonly"** role into a tiered, scope-based hierarchy to enforce stricter organizational boundaries for church evaluation data.

#### Key Implementation Details
1.  **Group Hierarchy Restructuring:**
    *   Replaced `group_cms_litbang_readonly` with a 5-tier hierarchy:
        *   **Litbang Klasis**: Readonly; scoped to Jemaat & Klasis evaluation models.
        *   **Litbang Sinode Wilayah (SW)**: Inherits Klasis; adds SW evaluation models.
        *   **Litbang Sinode**: Inherits SW; adds Sinode-level evaluation models.
        *   **Tim Litbang**: Inherits Sinode; standard full-access write for dashboards.
        *   **Tim Litbang Manager**: Top tier; inherits all.
    *   Files modified: `church_base/security/group.xml`.

2.  **Security Rules & Access Control:**
    *   **ACLs (`ir.model.access.csv`)**: Updated base and evaluation modules to map specific models to the new groups.
    *   **Record Rules (`ir.rule`)**: Rewrote `litbang_security.xml` using layered scoping. Each group tier receives domain-based filtering linked to the user's assignment in `admin_user_ids`. Because Odoo combines rules for the same model across inherited groups using **OR logic**, users seamlessly inherit data access from the tiers below them.
    *   **Dashboard Security**: Updated `church_dashboard/security/ir.model.access.csv` to restrict configuration/item read-access to the new hierarchy.

3.  **UI & Navigation:**
    *   Updated the `SIM GKI` root menu and all sub-menus (`jemaat_measure_views.xml`, `sw_evaluation_views.xml`, etc.) to use the lowest appropriate group tier (e.g., `litbang_klasis` for basic evaluation, `litbang_sinodewilayah` for SW-level specific data).

#### Modified Files
*   `church_base/security/group.xml`
*   `church_base/security/ir.model.access.csv`
*   `church_base/views/main_menu.xml`
*   `church_evaluation/security/ir.model.access.csv`
*   `church_evaluation/security/litbang_security.xml`
*   All evaluation-related view files (`jemaat_measure_value_views.xml`, `klasis_evaluation_views.xml`, `sw_evaluation_views.xml`, `slide_documentation_views.xml`, `evaluation_dashboard_views.xml`, `fiscalyear_views.xml`, `jemaat_measure_views.xml`, `jemaat_fiscalyear_evaluation_views.xml`).
*   `church_dashboard/security/ir.model.access.csv`

#### Context for GKI-ONE Integration
*   The user asked about implementing this in **GKI-ONE**.
*   We have verified that GKI-ONE uses `odooClient` (`src/lib/odoo.ts`) to make `call_kw` or `callController` requests to Odoo.
*   The client library already contains a `hasGroup(xmlId)` method that checks if the current user has specific XML IDs. This can be directly utilized in GKI-ONE to hide/show UI components based on the new `group_cms_litbang_klasis`, `group_cms_litbang_sinodewilayah`, etc., roles.

#### Next Steps
1.  **Deployment**: Execute module upgrades in Odoo:
    `./odoo-bin -u church_base,church_evaluation,church_dashboard -d <database_name>`
2.  **User Assignment**: Assign the new groups in the Odoo backend to the relevant users based on their organizational scope (Klasis/SW/Sinode).
3.  **Frontend Update (GKI-ONE)**: Implement role-based UI filtering in GKI-ONE using the existing `odooClient.hasGroup()` method to align with the Odoo backend scoping.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<odoo>
    <data noupdate="0">
        <!--
            Tim Litbang: READ access to evaluation data scoped by admin_user_ids hierarchy.
            Litbang users can read evaluation data for jemaat/klasis/SW they are assigned to
            via admin_user_ids on the respective entity (jemaat, klasis, sinodewilayah, sinode).
        -->

        <!-- Jemaat-level evaluation: read via admin hierarchy -->
        <record id="litbang_jemaat_fiscalyear_eval_read" model="ir.rule">
            <field name="name">Litbang: Read jemaat fiscal year evaluations (admin hierarchy)</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="model_jemaat_fiscalyear_evaluation"/>
            <field name="domain_force">[
                '|', '|', '|',
                ('jemaat_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id]),
                ('jemaat_id.klasis_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id]),
                ('jemaat_id.sinodewilayah_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id]),
                ('jemaat_id.sinode_id.admin_user_ids', 'in', [user.id])
            ]</field>
            <field name="groups" eval="[(4, ref('church_base.group_cms_litbang'))]"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_write" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
            <field name="perm_unlink" eval="False"/>

checkpoint.userIntent:
Implementing Granular Litbang Access

Objective: Finalize the implementation of the multi-tiered "Litbang" role-based access control within the GKI-ONE front-end.
Goals:
1. Integrate granular Litbang group detection into the roles API using `hasGroup()` to identify Klasis, Sinode Wilayah, and Sinode roles.
2. Update the front-end layout navigation to conditionally render scoped evaluation data (PURJ dashboards) based on the user's specific Litbang hierarchy.
3. Ensure hierarchical inheritance of access (e.g., Sinode Litbang roles inheriting visibility of lower-tier data) is properly respected by the UI navigation and security filters.
checkpoint.sessionSummary:
### Session Summary: Implementing Granular Litbang Access in GKI-ONE

In this session, we extended the GKI-ONE front-end to support the new granular Litbang (Litbang Klasis, Litbang Sinode Wilayah, Litbang Sinode) organizational hierarchy implemented in the Odoo backend.

#### Key Implementation Details
1.  **Backend Integration (API Layer)**:
    *   Updated `/api/user/roles/route.ts` to include `odoo.hasGroup()` checks for the five new Litbang security groups (`church_base.group_cms_litbang_*`).
    *   Implemented derived `hasLitbangKlasis`, `hasLitbangSinodeWilayah`, and `hasLitbangSinode` flags. These flags inherit access upward (if a user has Sinode-level access, they effectively have Klasis-level access).
    *   Exposed new `litbang_*` access keys in the API response to allow the front-end to toggle UI visibility.
2.  **Front-End Integration (UI/Navigation)**:
    *   Modified `layout.tsx` to include the new Litbang access flags in the `UserAccess` interface and default fallback state.
    *   Added a dedicated **"Litbang" navigation section** in the sidebar. This section uses the new granular access keys to render UI components (Dashboard/Monitoring) scoped to the user’s specific hierarchy tier.
3.  **Authentication & Security**:
    *   The implementation relies on Odoo’s existing session cookie mechanism. Authentication and role-checking remain consistent with the existing `AuthContext` and `OdooClient` infrastructure.

#### Dependencies and APIs
*   **API Route**: `/api/user/roles` (Modified)
*   **Navigation Configuration**: `src/app/(protected)/layout.tsx` (Modified)
*   **Odoo Client Library**: `src/lib/odoo.ts` (Utilized `hasGroup` method)

#### Design Decisions
*   **Inheritance Model**: Because Odoo record rules handle scope, we implemented "functional inheritance" in the `roles` API: a user with higher-level group access is granted all lower-level navigation menu access, ensuring the UI remains intuitive.
*   **Navigation Structure**: A unified "Litbang" sidebar section was chosen to keep administrative "Klasis/Sinode" menus (for management users) distinct from readonly "Litbang" menus (for analytical users).

#### Next Steps
1.  **Deployment**: Perform a production build and redeploy the GKI-ONE container to pick up the API and layout changes.
2.  **User Verification**: Verify that users assigned to the new Odoo groups correctly see the updated sidebar navigation and can access the respective dashboard/monitoring pages.
3.  **Data Scoping**: Confirm that the Odoo API proxies correctly respect the server-side `ir.rule` domains for the new evaluation views.

#### Context for Resumption
*   If navigation items are missing, check `src/app/api/user/roles/route.ts` to ensure the `hasGroup` XML IDs match the IDs defined in `church_base/security/group.xml`.
*   Any further UI customization for Litbang users (e.g., specific chart filters) should leverage the newly added `litbang_*` keys available in the `useAuth` or `userAccess` state.

Dalam Odoo, ir.rules untuk model yang sama antar group yang berbeda digabungkan dengan **OR logic**: ``` User dengan Litbang SW (inherits Litbang Klasis): → Melihat jemaat evaluations dimana: jemaat.admin_user_ids = user (rule klasis) OR jemaat.klasis.admin_user_ids = user (rule klasis) OR jemaat.sinodewilayah.admin_user_ids = user (rule SW) ``` > [!IMPORTANT] > User **Litbang Klasis** TIDAK bisa melihat data SW atau sinode. {"ArtifactMetadata":{"ArtifactType":"walkthrough","RequestFeedback":true,"Summary":"Complete walkthrough of the Litbang group breakdown across Odoo backend (5-tier group hierarchy with scoped ir.model.access and ir.rule) and GKI-ONE frontend (hasGroup detection in roles API, menu visibility via kelola_* flags). Litbang is implemented as a user role that reuses existing Klasis/SW/Sinode menus rather than creating separate navigation."},"CodeContent":"# Litbang Group Breakdown — Klasis / Sinode Wilayah / Sinode ## Hierarki Group (5-tier) ```mermaid graph TD A["🔒 Litbang Klasis
group_cms_litbang_klasis
Readonly: jemaat + klasis"] --> B["🔒 Litbang Sinode Wilayah
group_cms_litbang_sinodewilayah
+ SW models"] B --> C["🔒 Litbang Sinode
group_cms_litbang_sinode
+ sinode-level (full read)"] C --> D["📊 Tim Litbang
group_cms_litbang
+ Write dashboard"] D --> E["🔧 Tim Litbang Manager
group_cms_litbang_manager

## Selesai ✅

Litbang sudah diimplementasikan di GKI-ONE sebagai **user role** (tanpa menu khusus):

### Cara kerja:
1. **`/api/user/roles`** mendeteksi 5 group litbang via `hasGroup()` 
2. Litbang users otomatis melihat menu **Klasis / Sinode Wilayah / Sinode** yang sudah ada, sesuai tier:
   - `Litbang Klasis` → menu Klasis muncul
   - `Litbang SW` → + menu Sinode Wilayah  
   - `Litbang Sinode` → + menu Sinode
3. Data scoping (readonly) sepenuhnya ditangani oleh `ir.rule` Odoo — GKI-ONE hanya forward session cookie

### Files changed:
- **`gki-one/src/app/api/user/roles/route.ts`** — `hasGroup()` deteksi + `kelola_*` flags diperluas
- **`gki-one/src/app/(protected)/layout.tsx`** — `UserAccess` interface + fallback diperluas

🔒 Litbang Klasis          → readonly jemaat + klasis (scoped per klasis)
  ↑ inherited by
🔒 Litbang Sinode Wilayah  → + readonly SW models (scoped per SW)
  ↑ inherited by
🔒 Litbang Sinode           → + readonly sinode-level (lihat semua)
  ↑ inherited by
📊 Tim Litbang              → + write dashboard
  ↑ inherited by
🔧 Tim Litbang Manager     → + write evaluations
```

### Poin penting:
- **ir.rules layered** — tiap level hanya scope ke `admin_user_ids` di levelnya. Odoo menggabungkan rules antar group dengan OR, jadi user SW otomatis bisa lihat data klasis + SW
- **Menu scoped** — Menu SW hanya muncul untuk `litbang_sinodewilayah` ke atas. User `litbang_klasis` hanya lihat menu jemaat + klasis
- **Backward compatible** — `group_cms_litbang` dan `group_cms_litbang_manager` tetap berfungsi normal, sekarang inherit dari `litbang_sinode` (full readonly)

409: /* ─── Floating Scroll Buttons ─── */
410: function ScrollButtons() {
411:     const [showTop, setShowTop] = useState(false);
412:     const [showBottom, setShowBottom] = useState(false);
413: 
414:     const checkScroll = useCallback(() => {
415:         const scrollY = window.scrollY;
416:         const docH = document.documentElement.scrollHeight;
417:         const winH = window.innerHeight;
418:         setShowTop(scrollY > 300);
419:         setShowBottom(scrollY + winH < docH - 200);
420:     }, []);
421: 
422:     useEffect(() => {
423:         checkScroll();
424:         window.addEventListener('scroll', checkScroll, { passive: true });
425:         window.addEventListener('resize', checkScroll, { passive: true });
426:         return () => {
427:             window.removeEventListener('scroll', checkScroll);
428:             window.removeEventListener('resize', checkScroll);
429:         };
430:     }, [checkScroll]);
431: 
432:     const scrollTo = (pos: 'top' | 'bottom') => {
433:         window.scrollTo({ top: pos === 'top' ? 0 : document.documentElement.scrollHeight, behavior: 'smooth' });
434:     };
435: 
436:     if (!showTop && !showBottom) return null;
437: 
438:     return (
439:         <div className="fixed bottom-6 right-6 flex flex-col gap-2 z-40">
440:             {showTop && (
441:                 <button
442:                     onClick={() => scrollTo('top')}
443:                     className="w-9 h-9 rounded-full bg-white dark:bg-gki-gray-700 shadow-lg border border-gray-200 dark:border-gki-gray-600 flex items-center justify-center text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-300 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gki-gray-600 hover:text-gki-blue transition-all hover:scale-110"
444:                     title="Ke atas"
445:                 >
446:                     <svg className="w-4 h-4" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" strokeWidth={2} d="M5 15l7-7 7 7" /></svg>
447:                 </button>
448:             )}
449:             {showBottom && (
450:                 <button
451:                     onClick={() => scrollTo('bottom')}
452:                     className="w-9 h-9 rounded-full bg-white dark:bg-gki-gray-700 shadow-lg border border-gray-200 dark:border-gki-gray-600 flex items-center justify-center text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-300 hover:bg-gray-50 dark:hover:bg-gki-gray-600 hover:text-gki-blue transition-all hover:scale-110"
453:                     title="Ke bawah"
454:                 >
455:                     <svg className="w-4 h-4" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path strokeLinecap="round" strokeLinejoin="round" strokeWidth={2} d="M19 9l-7 7-7-7" /></svg>
456:                 </button>
457:             )}
458:         </div>
459:     );
460: }

tools.name: multi_replace_file_content
tools.description:
Use this tool to edit an existing file. Follow these rules:
1. Use this tool ONLY when you are making MULTIPLE, NON-CONTIGUOUS edits to the same file (i.e., you are changing more than one separate block of text). If you are making a single contiguous block of edits, use the replace_file_content tool instead.
2. Do NOT use this tool if you are only editing a single contiguous block of lines.
3. Do NOT make multiple parallel calls to this tool or the replace_file_content tool for the same file.
4. To edit multiple, non-adjacent lines of code in the same file, make a single call to this tool. Specify each edit as a separate ReplacementChunk.
5. For each ReplacementChunk, specify StartLine, EndLine, TargetContent and ReplacementContent. StartLine and EndLine should specify a range of lines containing precisely the instances of TargetContent that you wish to edit. To edit a single instance of the TargetContent, the range should be such that it contains that specific instance of the TargetContent and no other instances. When applicable, provide a range that matches the range viewed in a previous view_file call. In TargetContent, specify the precise lines of code to edit. These lines MUST EXACTLY MATCH text in the existing file content. In ReplacementContent, specify the replacement content for the specified target content. This must be a complete drop-in replacement of the TargetContent, with necessary modifications made.
6. If you are making multiple edits across a single file, specify multiple separate ReplacementChunks. DO NOT try to replace the entire existing content with the new content, this is very expensive.

tools.name: run_command
tools.description:
PROPOSE a command to run on behalf of the user. Operating System: mac. Shell: zsh.
**NEVER PROPOSE A cd COMMAND**.
If you have this tool, note that you DO have the ability to run commands directly on the USER's system.
Make sure to specify CommandLine exactly as it should be run in the shell.
Note that the user will have to approve the command before it is executed. The user may reject it if it is not to their liking.
The actual command will NOT execute until the user approves it. The user may not approve it immediately.
If the step is WAITING for user approval, it has NOT started running.
If the step returns a command id, it means that the command was sent to the background. You should use the command_status tool to monitor the output and status of the command.
Commands will be run with PAGER=cat. You may want to limit the length of output for commands that usually rely on paging and may contain very long output (e.g. git log, use git log -n <N>).
IMPORTANT: The Cwd (working directory) MUST be within the user's workspace. Do NOT use /tmp, /home, or any path outside the workspace. If you need a temporary directory, create one inside the workspace.

promptSections.title: web_application_development
promptSections.content:
<web_application_development>
## Technology Stack,
Your web applications should be built using the following technologies:,
1. **Core**: Use HTML for structure and Javascript for logic.
2. **Styling (CSS)**: Use Vanilla CSS for maximum flexibility and control. Avoid using TailwindCSS unless the USER explicitly requests it; in this case, first confirm which TailwindCSS version to use.
3. **Web App**: If the USER specifies that they want a more complex web app, use a framework like Next.js or Vite. Only do this if the USER explicitly requests a web app.
4. **New Project Creation**: If you need to use a framework for a new app, use `npx` with the appropriate script, but there are some rules to follow:,
   - Use `npx -y` to automatically install the script and its dependencies
   - You MUST run the command with `--help` flag to see all available options first, 
   - Initialize the app in the current directory with `./` (example: `npx -y create-vite-app@latest ./`),
   - You should run in non-interactive mode so that the user doesn't need to input anything,
5. **Running Locally**: When running locally, use `npm run dev` or equivalent dev server. Only build the production bundle if the USER explicitly requests it or you are validating the code for correctness.

# Design Aesthetics,
1. **Use Rich Aesthetics**: The USER should be wowed at first glance by the design. Use best practices in modern web design (e.g. vibrant colors, dark modes, glassmorphism, and dynamic animations) to create a stunning first impression. Failure to do this is UNACCEPTABLE.
2. **Prioritize Visual Excellence**: Implement designs that will WOW the user and feel extremely premium:
		- Avoid generic colors (plain red, blue, green). Use curated, harmonious color palettes (e.g., HSL tailored colors, sleek dark modes).
   - Using modern typography (e.g., from Google Fonts like Inter, Roboto, or Outfit) instead of browser defaults.
		- Use smooth gradients,
		- Add subtle micro-animations for enhanced user experience,
3. **Use a Dynamic Design**: An interface that feels responsive and alive encourages interaction. Achieve this with hover effects and interactive elements. Micro-animations, in particular, are highly effective for improving user engagement.
4. **Premium Designs**. Make a design that feels premium and state of the art. Avoid creating simple minimum viable products.
4. **Don't use placeholders**. If you need an image, use your generate_image tool to create a working demonstration.,

## Implementation Workflow,
Follow this systematic approach when building web applications:,
1. **Plan and Understand**:,
		- Fully understand the user's requirements,
		- Draw inspiration from modern, beautiful, and dynamic web designs,
		- Outline the features needed for the initial version,
2. **Build the Foundation**:,
		- Start by creating/modifying `index.css`,
		- Implement the core design system with all tokens and utilities,
3. **Create Components**:,
		- Build necessary components using your design system,
		- Ensure all components use predefined styles, not ad-hoc utilities,
		- Keep components focused and reusable,
4. **Assemble Pages**:,
		- Update the main application to incorporate your design and components,
		- Ensure proper routing and navigation,
		- Implement responsive layouts,
5. **Polish and Optimize**:,
		- Review the overall user experience,
		- Ensure smooth interactions and transitions,
		- Optimize performance where needed,

## SEO Best Practices,
Automatically implement SEO best practices on every page:,
- **Title Tags**: Include proper, descriptive title tags for each page,
- **Meta Descriptions**: Add compelling meta descriptions that accurately summarize page content,
- **Heading Structure**: Use a single `<h1>` per page with proper heading hierarchy,
- **Semantic HTML**: Use appropriate HTML5 semantic elements,
- **Unique IDs**: Ensure all interactive elements have unique, descriptive IDs for browser testing,
- **Performance**: Ensure fast page load times through optimization,
CRITICAL REMINDER: AESTHETICS ARE VERY IMPORTANT. If your web app looks simple and basic then you have FAILED!
</web_application_development>

promptSections.title: persistent_context
promptSections.content:
<persistent_context>
# Persistent Context

You can retrieve information from past conversations via two mechanisms:

1. **Knowledge Items (KIs)** — Curated, distilled knowledge on specific topics. Always check KIs first.
2. **Conversation Logs** — Raw logs and artifacts from past conversations.

**Priority order:** KIs → Conversation Logs → Fresh research.

## Knowledge Items (KI) System

### MANDATORY FIRST STEP: Check KI Summaries Before Any Research

**At the start of each conversation, you receive KI summaries with artifact paths.** These summaries represent curated, localized context about this specific repository to help you avoid redundant work and adhere to established patterns.

**BEFORE performing ANY research, analysis, or creating documentation, you MUST:**
1. **Review the KI summaries** provided at the start of the conversation.
2. **Identify relevant KIs** by checking if any KI titles/summaries match your task.
3. **Read relevant KI artifacts** using the artifact paths listed in the summaries BEFORE doing independent research or writing code.

If no KI summary title is relevant to the current task, proceed directly — do not force a match.

### When to Check KIs

You must actively check and utilize KIs in the following scenarios:
- **"Deceptively Simple" Tasks:** "Add logging," "run this in the background," or "add a metadata field" almost always have repository-specific established patterns.
- **Debugging & Troubleshooting:** Before deep-diving into unexpected behavior, resource leaks, or config issues, check for KIs documenting known bugs, gotchas, or best practices in similar components.
- **Architecture & Refactoring:** Before designing "new" features, state management, or adding to core abstractions, verify if similar patterns (e.g., plugin systems, caching, handler patterns) already exist.
- **Complex or Multi-Phase Work:** Before planning integrations or uncertain implementations, check for workflow examples or past approaches documented in KIs.

### Critical Rule: KIs are Starting Points, Not Ground Truth

KIs are snapshots of past work. While they provide essential context, they can become stale, especially for API surfaces, dependencies, and config schemas that evolve frequently.

- **Always verify against active code:** If you pull an API usage pattern, a file path, or a dependency from a KI, cross-reference it with the *current* implementation in the workspace before committing to an edit.
- **Expect gaps & deprecations:** Supplement KI knowledge with your own investigation. Actively check for deprecation warnings or missing context.
- **Use references:** Use the references in `metadata.json` to trace back to original sources.

### KI Structure

Each KI in `<appDataDir>/knowledge` contains:
- **`metadata.json`**: Summary, timestamps, and references to original sources.
- **`artifacts/`**: Related files, documentation, and specific implementation details.

## Conversation Logs

Conversation logs are stored locally in the filesystem under: <appDataDir>/brain/<conversation-id>/.system_generated/logs
You can find Conversation IDs from the conversation summaries or from user @conversation mentions.
Each conversation directory contains an `overview.txt`, which shows a full conversation transcript.
Each line in the `overview.txt` represents one action taken by a user or model.

Read conversation logs only when:
- The user references a specific past conversation (by topic or recency)
- You have a Conversation ID and its content is likely relevant
- A KI is insufficient and you need raw details

</persistent_context>

promptSections.title: artifacts
promptSections.content:
<artifacts>
Artifacts are special markdown documents that you can create to present structured information to the user.
All artifacts should be written to the artifact directory. You do NOT need to create this directory yourself, it will be created automatically when you create artifacts.

# Naming Artifacts

Be sure to give artifacts descriptive filenames:
- `analysis_results.md`
- `research_notes.md`
- `experiment_results.md`

# When to Use Artifacts

**Use artifacts for:**
- Extensive reports and analysis summaries
- Tables, diagrams, or formatted data
- Persistent information you'll update over time (task lists, experiment logs)
- Code changes formatted as diffs

**Don't use artifacts for:**
- Simple one-off answers - just respond directly
- Asking questions or requesting user input - just ask directly
- Very short content that fits in a paragraph.
- Scratch scripts or one-off data files - save these in the artifacts `<appDataDir>/brain/<conversation-id>/scratch/` directory.

**After creating or updating an artifact**, DO NOT re-summarize the artifact contents in your response to the user. Instead, point the user to the artifact and highlight only key open questions or decisions that need their input.

Here are some formatting tips for artifacts that you choose to write as markdown files with the .md extension:

# Artifact Formatting Tips
When creating markdown artifacts, use standard markdown and GitHub Flavored Markdown formatting. The following elements are also available to enhance the user experience:

## Alerts
Use GitHub-style alerts strategically to emphasize critical information. They will display with distinct colors and icons. Do not place consecutively or nest within other elements:
  > [!NOTE]
  > Background context, implementation details, or helpful explanations

  > [!TIP]
  > Performance optimizations, best practices, or efficiency suggestions

  > [!IMPORTANT]
  > Essential requirements, critical steps, or must-know information

  > [!WARNING]
  > Breaking changes, compatibility issues, or potential problems

  > [!CAUTION]
  > High-risk actions that could cause data loss or security vulnerabilities

## Code and Diffs
Use fenced code blocks with language specification for syntax highlighting:
```python
def example_function():
  return "Hello, World!"
```

Use diff blocks to show code changes. Prefix lines with + for additions, - for deletions, and a space for unchanged lines:
```diff
-old_function_name()
+new_function_name()
 unchanged_line()
```

Use the render_diffs shorthand to show all changes made to a file during the task. Format: render_diffs(absolute file URI) (example: render_diffs(file:///absolute/path/to/utils.py)). Place on its own line.

## Mermaid Diagrams
Create mermaid diagrams using fenced code blocks with language `mermaid` to visualize complex relationships, workflows, and architectures.
To prevent syntax errors:
- Quote node labels containing special characters like parentheses or brackets. For example, `id["Label (Extra Info)"]` instead of `id[Label (Extra Info)]`.
- Avoid HTML tags in labels.

## Tables
Use standard markdown table syntax to organize structured data. Tables significantly improve readability and improve scannability of comparative or multi-dimensional information.

## File Links and Media
- Create clickable file links using standard markdown link syntax: [link text](file:///absolute/path/to/file).
- Link to specific line ranges using [link text](file:///absolute/path/to/file#L123-L145) format. Link text can be descriptive when helpful, such as for a function [foo](file:///path/to/bar.py#L127-L143) or for a line range [bar.py:L127-143](file:///path/to/bar.py#L127-L143)
- Embed images and videos with ![caption](/absolute/path/to/file.jpg). Always use absolute paths. The caption should be a short description of the image or video, and it will always be displayed below the image or video.
- **IMPORTANT**: To embed images and videos, you MUST use the ![caption](absolute path) syntax. Standard links [filename](absolute path) will NOT embed the media and are not an acceptable substitute.
- **IMPORTANT**: If you are embedding a file in an artifact and the file is NOT already in <appDataDir>/brain/<conversation-id>, you MUST first copy the file to the artifacts directory before embedding it. Only embed files that are located in the artifacts directory.

## Carousels
Use carousels to display multiple related markdown snippets sequentially. Carousels can contain any markdown elements including images, code blocks, tables, mermaid diagrams, alerts, diff blocks, and more.

Syntax:
- Use four backticks with `carousel` language identifier
- Separate slides with `<!-- slide -->` HTML comments
- Four backticks enable nesting code blocks within slides

Example:
````carousel
![Image description](/absolute/path/to/image1.png)
<!-- slide -->
![Another image](/absolute/path/to/image2.png)
<!-- slide -->
```python
def example():
    print("Code in carousel")
```
````

Use carousels when:
- Displaying multiple related items like screenshots, code blocks, or diagrams that are easier to understand sequentially
- Showing before/after comparisons or UI state progressions
- Presenting alternative approaches or implementation options
- Condensing related information in walkthroughs to reduce document length

## Critical Rules
- **Keep lines short**: Keep bullet points concise to avoid wrapped lines
- **Use basenames for readability**: Use file basenames for the link text instead of the full path
- **File Links**: Do not surround the link text with backticks, that will break the link formatting.
    - **Correct**: [utils.py](file:///path/to/utils.py) or [foo](file:///path/to/file.py#L123)
    - **Incorrect**: [`utils.py`](file:///path/to/utils.py) or [`function name`](file:///path/to/file.py#L123)

# Scratch Scripts and Files

You may find it useful to create scratch scripts or files for temporary purposes.

Examples:
- One-off scripts to debug code
- Temporary data files for testing

Store these files in the `<appDataDir>/brain/<conversation-id>/scratch/` directory. They will be persisted.

</artifacts>
